newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL LAUNCH SPECTACULAR COMEBACK AS BARCELONA CRUMBLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL LAUNCH SPECTACULAR COMEBACK AS BARCELONA CRUMBLE.

text.p: Real Madrid took a decisive step to their 27th Spanish league title on Wednesday after launching a spectacular comeback from two early goals to beat bottom-placed Sevilla 4-2.
The win came as second-placed Barcelona crashed 3-1 at Valladolid, leaving Fabio Capello's side 10 points clear at the top with just eight games left to play.
It was the first time in nearly 15 years that Real had come back from two goals down.
Things were looking good for Barcelona after Real went behind and Ronaldo had given Bobby Robson's side a fourth-minute lead.
But the Catalans wilted under continuous pressure, and were sunk by two goals by diminutive striker Victor Fernandez.
The evening could have been even worse for Barcelona, who had stood to lose second place and with it Spain's second European Cup place for next season, if Real Betis had beaten struggling Zaragoza.
But Betis threw away a two-goal lead for the second successive home game, and had to settle for a 2-2 draw that leaves them one point adrift of Barcelona.
